title: C4458 — Radio Transceiver Module (RTM)
introduction:
The airwaves get the glamorous part, but a radio transceiver module still has a wired side. This reference maps its ground, remote radio-frequency receiver connection, medium-speed network connections and supply. I use those function labels to keep the different jobs straight: a receiver connection and a network connection are not interchangeable just because both carry information.

Begin with the identification table, then match a label in the vertical cavity column to its Cavity row. Read across that row for the circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal entry. The shaded position aligns with the blank circuit row; it is an unused position in this reference rather than an invitation to add a wire. The service table below provides the pigtail catalog entries.

This is a guide to reading the connector map. Physical viewing direction, access, probe placement, electrical test conditions and replacement methods belong to separate procedures. Gauge conventions and catalog codes remain as printed, and the pigtail entries alone do not establish which part to install.

edits.why: I use the vertical cavity column, broader lower housing outline and features along the drawing’s right edge to keep my place in the illustration. Match the cavity labels to the table rather than counting only the unshaded positions. The drawing’s page orientation does not establish a physical terminal-side or wire-side view.

Cavity gives the drawn position; Circuit Number identifies the electrical circuit. Read the complete row to distinguish ground, receiver, network and supply functions. The network’s high and low labels distinguish connections rather than test outcomes. The blank circuit row and shaded cavity agree on an unused position; neither establishes a wiring fault.

A pigtail is a connector supplied with attached repair leads. Keep each catalog row’s gauge, material, service-part and engineering-shell information together. The shared shell entry identifies a common catalog detail; it does not settle pigtail interchangeability or provide a replacement method.
